diagnosis: kernel_check_invariants aborted with 'binary clause escaped propagation': INVARIANT: unit binary (-18 -1) at level 0 with head 16 == trail size 16, i.e. a claimed root fixpoint leaving a unit clause unpropagated. Fourth member of the escaped-unit family after corpus 004 (decide on an unpropagated trail), 005 (chronological backjump mis-leveling) and 006 (a lost learned-clause handoff), and again a DIFFERENT cause: a clause ADDED BEHIND THE PROPAGATION CURSOR. Pinned with a temporary probe in kernel_add_binary_clause, which printed `ADDBIN-STALE: (-1 -18) false -18 at trailpos 13, head 15, size 16, other value 0` -- the binary is added while 18 is already true at level 0 at trail position 13, but propagate_head is 15, so -18's watch list has already been scanned. Propagation is trail-driven: it reaches a clause only through the watch list of a literal it is currently scanning off the trail, so a clause added over an already-scanned false literal is never looked at again, and the next drain still reports a fixpoint. V5 Sweep reaches this because its emission deliberately keeps units unpropagated for the whole pass (Kissat parity) while congruence_rup_chain's probing propagation fixes literals underneath the pair it is about to add -- so the `k.value(e.a) != 0 || k.value(e.b) != 0` guard at the top of sweep_emit_round's loop is already STALE by the time kernel_add_binary_clause runs. NOT a soundness bug: the clause is watched correctly, so assigning the other literal still fires a conflict; it is a missed propagation plus a violated kernel fixpoint invariant, which aborts every assertions-on build. Fixed 2026-08-11 in the kernel rather than in Sweep, so it covers every adder: kernel_add_binary_clause and kernel_add_large_clause (hence kernel_replace_clause) rewind propagate_head to the earliest already-scanned false literal of the clause they are adding. Gated to `level == 0 && !conflict_valid`, because ConflictAnalysis is the one caller that adds above the root and adds a clause whose literals are all false by construction -- re-arming there would rewind the cursor over the whole trail on every conflict, where the Backjump that must follow already resets it to the level boundary. Counted as `propagation re-arms` on the `c chrono` line; this case fires it exactly once. THIS CASE: 07dccc2 aborts in ~2 s under --random-policy in either proof format; the fixed binary answers UNSAT, the proof checks, and the per-step invariant oracle is clean for the whole walk.
